messages:
Sam W: quick RFC follow-up: RFC-421 suggested active/active across regions with policy-based routing for residency. a few open questions on session affinity, KV cache replication, and failover semantics. thoughts?
Maria L: +1. main constraint is 'hard residency' customers — their PII+logs must never leave region. can't replicate raw blobs.
Charlie P: that means we can't do full KV replication for those tenants. options: 1) per-tenant single-region KV + cross-region proxying, 2) replicate encrypted blobs with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM), or 3) fall back to remote read-only model variant.
Tina K: option 2 adds key management and HSM complexities. also more latency for decrypt/serve. option 1 is simpler operationally but hurts HA on region outage unless we have clear failover runbook.
Sam W: how would failover work for single-region KV? if region A goes down and tenant is residency-bound to A, do we: a) keep tenant offline until A recovers, b) failover to a quarantined read-only in region B, or c) offer opt-in cross-region failover?
Maria L: I'd push for opt-in cross-region failover with explicit acceptance in contract. default must be offline. we need an API flag on tenant profile: "allow_cross_region_failover": true/false.
Charlie P: agree. implementation: tag requests with residency attribute at edge, ensure routing respects it. session affinity token should include region tag so we don't accidentally route sticky sessions elsewhere. e.g., cookie: "aff=eu-central;res=eu;v=2".
Tina K: about KV cache: for non-residency tenants we can do async replication with bounded staleness (raft/CDC). for residency tenants, keep a lightweight proxy that forwards cache-miss to primary region rather than replicating. reduces leakage risk.
Sam W: what about model weights and runtime? models are global. is serving model weights in a different region a residency violation?
Maria L: model weights aren't user data by default. but embeddings/logs produced by inference are. and if we run the model in-region on customer request, we must ensure logs/outputs are persisted only in-region. that means per-request wiring to local logging sinks and not forwarding traces to global observability unless scrubbed.
Charlie P: operationally we should implement a residency marker in traces/spans and have the observability pipeline drop or redirect those spans. simple env var at runtime won't work since replicas may be multi-region. explicitly set resource.residency on the span.
Tina K: testing: add chaos tests that kill region and validate opt-in tenants either stay offline or failover-only-if-flag set. add e2e that ensures no residency-tagged artifacts are visible in other regions' S3/logs.
Sam W: rollout plan idea: 1) add tenant profile flag + routing enforcement, 2) implement proxy-on-miss for residency KV, 3) residency markers for logs/traces, 4) opt-in cross-region failover feature behind feature flag, 5) docs + sales contract updates.
Maria L: +1. timeline? Can we aim for an alpha in staging next quarter?
Tina K: engineering estimate: steps 1-3 approx 6-8 sprint-weeks (infra+runtime). step 4 another 2-3 sprints for safety and runbooks.
Charlie P: one more: SLOs for failover. we need a clear degradation contract (latency, availability) when serving from remote region. also cost implications for cross-region egress. put those into the SLA matrix.
Sam W: noted. I'll open a follow-up ticket to capture opt-in wording and SLO deltas.
infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout triggered for feature/residency-routing to staging at 2024-11-02T18:04:00Z :rocket:
Sam W: thanks — will add test plan to the ticket and sync with legal on contract language. :thumbsup:
